originality.rationale: The new claim concerns the endpoint p=1 in finite real weighted Lorentz spaces, the exact minimal norm of the specified signed centering operator for arbitrary positive decreasing weights, and the sharp dimension-three-only norm-one phenomenon. In Randrianantoanina arXiv:math/9702214, Section 3 expressly treats p>1 and its key property (Q) fails at p=1. The 1996 paper deals chiefly with complex and disjoint-support cases. Published abstracts of Jameson 1999 concern norms of positive operators and of Kaminska-Lee-Lewicki 2009 give an existence-set equivalence rather than this exact quantitative classification. Four targeted the published mathematical-record index searches yielded no matching statement. Two highly plausible full texts were inaccessible, so originality is not asserted absolutely.
residual_risks: Jameson (1999) on d(w,1) operator norms was accessible only bibliographically/through summaries; some signed-operator specialization or full general principle could cover the formula.
Kaminska-Lee-Lewicki (2009) covers one-complementation of d(w,1); its full paper could contain the same hyperplane/weight threshold as a corollary of uninspected characterizations.
the published mathematical-record index semantic retrieval and web search do not establish global uniqueness; older offline/unindexed work may contain equivalent statements.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete parameter/dimension classification of relative projection constants for the permutation-symmetric zero-sum hyperplane of the full finite weighted-rearrangement Lorentz endpoint family. The p=1 case has a genuine three-dimensional exceptional phase boundary w1=w2+w3, ruled out in every higher dimension for all positive weights. Concrete applications include deciding one-complementability of a canonical hyperplane for any finite decreasing weight profile.
